# Display

Archivo Bold set wide, for the one title that is the point of a screen.

Status: Stable. Semantic versioning applies: nothing breaks without a deprecation first.

Archivo Bold at `wdth` 118. A heading here is a shape cut to fill its panel; the width, not a colour, is what keeps it out of the generic tight-grotesque register. One per screen at most — page titles in a working view are `Heading level={1}`.

## Usage

### When to use

- An empty state, an onboarding panel or the page that introduces a tool.
- The signature display-cut class, on a filled panel, once per page.

### When not to

- Page titles in a working view. Use [Heading](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-typography-heading--overview.md).
- A label that says what kind of block this is. Use [Rotulo](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-typography-rotulo--overview.md).

### Do and don’t

- Do: Use one per screen at most.
- Don’t: Set display-cut on light cloth; it reads as a sticker, not appliqué.

### Content

- Keep it to a few words; it is set at up to 76px.

## API

### `Display` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `"h1" \| "h2" \| "p"` | `h1` | The heading element. Defaults to h1; the visual register does not change. |

`className`, `ref`, `id` and the other DOM props go to `<h1 data-slot="display">`.

Types: `DisplayProps`

## Accessibility

Nothing in it takes focus, so there is no keyboard table.

### Mola handles

- Renders an `h1` by default, or an `h2` or `p` through `as`, without changing the look.

### You handle

- Use `as` so the element matches the outline: at most one `h1` per page.

### Testing status

- Automated, jsdom: each of its 2 stories is rendered and checked with axe on every pull request.
- Automated, browser: every story is checked in Chromium with axe, colour contrast included, in both themes, and for overflow at 390px.
- Keyboard in unit tests: not applicable.
- Screen readers: not yet tested by hand.
